ledger.title: The corpus applies Fluent Bit-tree pins, now including the derived channel range, to standalone Monkey units
ledger.text: Registered by CELL-GUARD-RESULT-RANGE-CHECKED. The corpus route evaluates every pin over its Fluent Bit source root (`lib/monkey/...` sites), while its Monkey units come from Monkey's standalone libevent build (`mk_core/...`). A pinned declaration of a Monkey function, now including mk_event_channel_create's pin-derived `nonnull_result_range(-1, 0)` (derived over Fluent Bit's epoll unit), is therefore in force at the corpus's Monkey callers on the strength of another tree's body. The range also holds for the libevent backend from its body alone (census part 1), and no corpus creator is read today (mk_sched_launch_worker_loop :365 and mk_server_create :115/:136 are refused at the access gate first). DISCHARGE: pins of Monkey functions evaluated over the tree the analysed unit comes from (a Monkey-tree identity, or a derivation at the corpus's Monkey compile database), or held for units outside the pinned tree, with a measurement showing the corpus's rows.

AMENDED (CELL-GUARD-RESULT-RANGE-CHECKED, 2026-11-03): the result-set form this reading needs exists (USER DECISION 2026-11-03 option C, `result_set`, contract specification C09.4) and pipe, epoll_ctl and open are declared C library result sets (quirin-provider-libc libc/result_sets.qv, flexible under libc-c-standard-abi); the pin-time derivation (rule 38e) can derive a timer result set from them. What remains: declaring `timerfd_create` (-1 | [0, MAX], Linux timerfd_create(2)), which the libc placement test refuses until providers/quirin-provider-libc/libc-names.txt is regenerated over a build whose units include <sys/timerfd.h> (the pinned corpus builds Monkey with libevent); a derived `mk_event_timeout_create` set; and the validity witness read through it (rule 38e's exact class reading in place of W43's `facts` table at a cell witness).
